items.question: Do the researchers discuss limitations, threats to validity, assumptions, or scope boundaries?
items.rationale: The paper explicitly bounds the implementation to the original mission profile, identifies component modeling as work in progress, and discusses training, communication, and legacy-work limitations.
evidence: At the time of publication of this article, the implementation of the SeaLion mission architecture was performed to the prior mission parameters where the SeaLion CubeSat was designed for a short lifespan compared to now greatly extended planned lifespan.
Components is currently a work in progress at time of publication of this article and will be addressed with future required work.

Current guides are lists of definitions and format guides rather than a step-by-step tutorial on using the approach, which has caused confusion among members that attempted to learn the material by themselves.

items.question: Is the nanosatellite/CubeSat mission context and lifecycle stage described clearly enough to interpret applicability?
items.rationale: The mission, platform, payloads, organizations, launch profile, and architecture-development stage are described in detail.
evidence: The SeaLion CubeSat mission is a joint project between Old Dominion University (ODU), the United States Coast Guard Academy (USCGA), and the Air Force Institute of Technology (AFIT).
The end goal is to produce a 3U CubeSat consisting of three payloads for on-orbit validation.
The content presented in this article is based on the prior mission profile from the launch at WFF into VLEO.

items.question: Are the MBSE method, language, toolchain, model artifacts, and system boundary described clearly enough to support replication or comparison?
items.rationale: The paper names the language, rationale, file/folder structure, artifact types, examples, and generation mechanisms sufficiently for comparison and partial replication.
evidence: M30ML was chosen for its lightweight human and machine-readable textual syntax, file-based model interchange support (for persisting models directly on the local filesystem), ability to generate both textual and graphical views, and relatively minimal overhead with modern doctools [29].
The SeaLion mission architecture is organized into two main folders of architecture and of components [13].
YAML files are automatically processed using templates language (e.g., Jinja2) via a build shell script.

items.question: Are claimed outcomes explicitly linked to MBSE artifacts, MBSE activities, or model-enabled process changes rather than asserted generically?
items.rationale: Claims about ease of use, traceability, documentation generation, consistency, and change accommodation are tied to YAML/M30ML models, generated diagrams/tables, templates, and docs-as-code workflow.
evidence: These tools generate documents via its own code for easy presentation on a local file system without any proprietary software while keeping the model content format-agnostic.
Figure 20 is a UML diagram of mapping of user stories to data structures generated from the YAML file shown in Figure 19.
This means that any changes made to the SeaLion mission architecture model can immediately be used to generate new documents.

items.question: Is evidence provided for claimed outcomes, such as metrics, baseline comparison, case-study results, executable simulation results, model checks, stakeholder evaluation, reuse evidence, integration/test results, or flight/operational data?
items.rationale: The paper provides case-study artifacts, generated views, repository availability, and anecdotal training observations, but no measured baseline comparison, model checking, integration-test, or flight/operational evidence.
evidence: Multiple team members of the SeaLion mission have been able to quickly learn the methodology of using the docs-as-code approach within a short training session with an experienced member.
A conference proceeding manuscript presented in AIAA SciTech 2023 was created purely by a docs-as-code format [4].
Implementation of the overall mission architecture has been successful for the original mission profile.

items.question: Are requirements, verification, validation, design decisions, or lifecycle gates traced to model artifacts when such traceability is central to the paper?
items.rationale: Traceability is central and is implemented through derivedFrom fields linking references, stakeholder needs, user stories, and data structures, with generated UML mappings.
evidence: For the mission architecture shown in Figure 9, generally data structures are derived from user stories. Furthermore, user stories are subsequently derived from stakeholder needs with their respective references.
The derived from field is used to tie back the data structure to a user story YAML file should it be applicable.
Figure 16 is an excerpt of mapping of stakeholder needs to user stories.

items.question: Are model availability, open-source assets, reusable packages, data exchange mechanisms, or sufficient implementation details reported to assess reproducibility and toolchain continuity?
items.rationale: The paper reports a public repository, local plain-text YAML persistence, Git-compatible workflow, non-proprietary document generation, and model-to-document continuity mechanisms.
evidence: The SeaLion mission architecture and methodology is available in a publicly accessible repository.
Documents should be in plain text as to be compatible with modern distributed version control system (e.g., Git) and for ease of use;
Proprietary services are not required to generate documentation, modify documentation, or modify models.

quality_checklist.overall_rationale: Strong reporting of venue, CubeSat context, method/toolchain, traceability, and reproducible docs-as-code artifacts; evidence for outcomes is mainly artifact-based and anecdotal rather than quantified, tested, or operational.

bibliographic_review_management.status_rationale: Kept as supporting because it is a CubeSat MBSE/docs-as-code case study with reusable modeling and toolchain evidence, but it is not an EPS-specific modeling or verification study.
bibliographic_review_management.citation: Chiu, K.; Marquez, S.; Asundi, S. Model Based Systems Engineering with a Docs-as-Code Approach for the SeaLion CubeSat Project. Systems 2023, 11, 320. https://doi.org/10.3390/systems11070320
bibliographic_review_management.title: Model Based Systems Engineering with a Docs-as-Code Approach for the SeaLion CubeSat Project

RQ1.rationale: Directly addresses general CubeSat mission/flight-software architecture modeling with lightweight YAML artifacts and limited training, but not EPS behavior modeling.

RQ2.rationale: Claims system-level reliability, reproducibility, traceability, and integration benefits from MBSE/docs-as-code, but these outcomes are not EPS-specific and are weakly evidenced.

RQ3.rationale: Includes general verification/validation user stories and satellite-health data structures including battery fields, but no EPS-specific pre-physical verification procedure, simulation, or model checking is reported.

bibliographic_review_management.lineage_overlap_notes: The article states it expands a 2023 AIAA SciTech conference proceeding; no other papers, prior extractions, sources.bib, or lineage files were read under silo rules.

implementation_pathway_tailoring.approach_classification_rationale: The study uses MBSE artifacts as the source of truth and enhances them with docs-as-code practices, Git-compatible plain text, templates, and automated document/view generation rather than using a conventional monolithic MBSE tool alone.

M30ML has lightweight YAML syntax and minimal overhead with modern doctools.
Models should persist on a local filesystem and not require proprietary software or cloud services.

Formatting-agnostic model content reduces duplicate documentation work.

RQ1: A CubeSat mission can be modeled at a general, low-overhead level using M30ML/YAML files for references, stakeholder needs, user stories, and data structures, with derivedFrom links providing traceability.

The approach captures expected ground-operator behaviors and flight-software data structures without requiring executable subsystem behavior models, making it suitable for teams with limited training but not for detailed EPS behavior analysis.
Component/DOF extensions aim to generalize CubeSat component, interface, BOM, and assembly modeling, but they were still under development.
RQ2: Reliability/mission-success benefits are mostly aspirational and system-level, motivated by high university CubeSat failure rates; no flight or test evidence links the model to reliability outcomes.

Reproducibility is the strongest outcome: public repository, plain-text YAML, local filesystem persistence, no proprietary services, and generated documentation are clearly linked to the model/toolchain.
Integrability is addressed through traceability and planned N2/interface/assembly artifacts, but integration-test evidence is not provided.
RQ3: Verification and validation are represented generally through MBSE activities, user stories, and data structures such as Satellite Health Data Packet, but not as formal EPS verification procedures.

Battery health and temperature fields are modeled as satellite-health telemetry, providing EPS-adjacent information before operation, but no EPS simulation, model check, power-budget verification, or hardware test integration is reported.
Planned N2 charts could support pre-physical interface review, including electrical interfaces, but the paper treats this as future work rather than demonstrated EPS verification.

author_stated_limitations_gaps: The implemented mission architecture reflected the prior mission parameters, not the newly changed mission profile.
The components folder was work in progress at publication.
Component data-structure use was still partly in contention.
Training material needed improvement because current guides were not step-by-step tutorials.
Communication with subsystem team members was necessary and unavailable contributors could delay architecture completion.
Legacy design decisions made before the architecture model had to be gathered and adapted.
extractor_identified_limitations_gaps: No EPS-specific architecture, requirements set, behavioral model, power-budget model, or verification procedure is demonstrated.
No quantitative evidence, baseline comparison, integration-test result, model-checking result, simulation output, or flight/operational data supports the claimed reliability or efficiency outcomes.
The method lacks demonstrated executable semantics, limiting behavioral verification claims.
The public repository is reported but was not inspected under silo rules, so reproducibility is assessed only from the paper's description.
N2 chart generation and component/interface modeling are partly future work, not validated integration evidence.

direct_evidence_quotes.quote: Through model-based systems engineering (MBSE), the SeaLion mission architecture team was able to create models, as opposed to documents, that serve as the authoritative source of truth for the conduction of system engineer activities [1].
